bundleBaseline.measuredAt: 2026-08-30, after the structure reading surfaced in the connection explorer and the ninth and tenth depth families landed
bundleBaseline.figuresAreSnapshots: verify-release-docs.mjs asserts each rawKb is within its budget; it never re-measures the build, so these figures are snapshots that drift silently. Re-measure before quoting any of these, and read the BUDGET, not the figure, as the enforced quantity. These six were measured with gzip -9 on the built assets straight after pnpm build.
bundleBaseline.entryBudgetRationale: Budget stays 1024 KiB. It was set when wave 3 doubled the curated atlas (176 -> 371 islands), because the growth is L0 atlas DATA rather than a new runtime: atlas.ts loads eagerly on purpose so the first frame is a real map with no round trip, and every island's question (`qfocus`) must be present offline since the chart's hover card and the connection-field search both read it from the L0 projection via api/fallback.ts. Deferring qfocus to atlas-detail was measured (36% of the L0 payload; it lands the entry at 914KiB) and rejected -- it leaves the no-server readable twin with a questionless island card, which the resilience invariant forbids. What DID move is the seed structure catalogue: structures.ts plus its wave expansion modules reached the entry through static imports of api/structureFallback from two eager screens and through a two-line `slugOfOp` helper that used to live in the same module. That data is needed only once a reader opens the structure lens, so it now loads through import() as its own chunk. Note the failure that preceded this: the wave-3 structure mappings (commit c97e625) pushed the entry to 1108.9 KiB -- 85 KiB over -- and it went unnoticed because `pnpm build` is in neither `pnpm -r test` nor `pnpm typecheck`, so every gate stayed green while the release build was broken. Naming the modules in guardEntryChunk's ENTRY_FORBIDDEN list is what makes the next occurrence say what leaked instead of only that the total grew.
bundleBaseline.budgetOnMerge: The merge kept 1024 on purpose rather than by letting git pick. The structures branch carried 900, sized for a 188-island atlas, and its own text argued the budget had not been raised to fit new data. Only one side changed that line, so git took 1024 with no conflict -- a budget relaxed by an automatic merge that nobody decided. The merged tree measures 834.2 KiB, which fits under both, so 900 was available. It was not taken: the 1024 rationale above is a written decision about an atlas of THIS size, turning on L0 atlas data that must load eagerly and cannot defer qfocus, and reverting to 900 would leave 65.8 KiB of headroom for 383 islands while re-adopting a number chosen for 188. 900 is recorded here as what the smaller atlas held to, not as a target to return to.
bundleBaseline.depthLayerRationale: Where the deferral shows its work, and the reason to record it rather than assume it. Seven depth families gave 56 of the 126 seed structures their own content -- origin, minimal form, canonical substrates in other disciplines, relations to other structures, and what each is mistaken for -- which is 193 substrates across 120 disciplines and 118 relations, and more than doubled the catalogue. Across that work the entry chunk moved 701.15 -> 710.52 kB, up 9.37, which is the depth type declarations and nothing else, while structureFallback went 238.37 -> 560.14, up 321.77: content grew 34x faster in the deferred chunk than in the eager one. Merging wave 3 then moved both again, the entry to 854.25 for 195 more islands of eager L0 data and structureFallback to 670.69 for wave 3's structure patches. The number to watch is still the ratio rather than the entry size -- if a later edit makes it fall, something has been statically imported back onto the first-paint path, which is exactly how the wave-5 build failed the guard over a two-line helper. 2026-08-30: two more families (field-and-flow, observation-and-absence) took the catalogue to 80 of 126 structures with depth -- 280 canonical substrates across 161 disciplines, 185 relations -- and the same content finally reached a reader: the connection explorer now renders a structure's own origin, minimal form, quantities, substrates, relations and mistakenFor on desktop and mobile through a lazily opened StructureReading. The entry chunk moved 854.25 -> 859.55 kB, which is the reading component and its wiring; structureFallback moved 670.69 -> 832.03 kB for the 16 new patches and a reverse relation index. The ratio held: 30x more content in the deferred chunk than in the eager one, and ENTRY_FORBIDDEN now also names the structures-depth-* modules so a family file can never be statically imported back onto first paint.
